subject: SIG: Medexa data lifecycle & training — follow-up
messages:
From: Sara Khan <sara.khan@medexa.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: security@medexa.com
Date: Thu, 10 Apr 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up — clarification on prompt/log retention and training

Jonas,

Thanks for taking this. The SIG we received asks a few follow-ups we want clarified for procurement:

- How long does Redwood retain raw prompt + response logs for hosted API customers by default?
- Are prompts or customer content ever used to continue-training or fine-tune public or internal models?
- Do you offer an opt-out for customers to prevent their content from being used for model training?
- For embeddings/reduced representations, do you keep originals? How are they purged?
- Can you provide evidence (policy excerpt or a redacted sample of logs) showing PII handling and redaction?

Procurement will need these answers to proceed. Can you also attach any SOC 2 or SIG evidence we can share with our legal team?

Best,
Sara Khan
Head of Security Operations
Medexa Health

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sara Khan <sara.khan@medexa.com>
Cc: maya.srinivasan@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Apr 2025 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — clarification on prompt/log retention and training

Sara — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; we'll follow up with a formal SIG response and evidence bundle attached.

1) Default retention (hosted API): Raw prompt & response payloads are retained for 30 days by default to support debugging, abuse detection, and quality monitoring. We maintain aggregated telemetry longer (90–180 days) depending on account activity.

2) Training on customer data: Redwood DOES NOT use customer content to train or improve public models by default. Training on customer content is strictly opt-in and only available under explicit contractual terms (enterprise addendum) and with additional controls (isolated datasets, encryption, and legal approvals).

3) Opt-out: Customers can opt out via an account setting for hosted plans; for enterprise customers we include a contractual no-training clause. Private and Dedicated deployments never send customer data to our shared training pipelines.

4) Embeddings and derived artifacts: Embeddings are treated as customer data; retention follows the same policy as other content. Deletion requests remove embeddings from live indexes and any backups per our retention schedule (see attached excerpt).

5) Evidence: I'm attaching an initial SIG reply PDF and a redacted prompt-log sample. We can also provide a SOC 2 Type II summary report stub. If Procurement needs a signed addendum preventing training, we can loop in Legal.

If you need a short written statement we can authorize for procurement/board review, I'll get Legal to provide one.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Security Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_sig_reply_v1.pdf

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: maya.srinivasan@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Apr 2025 08:31:00 -0700
Subject: Internal — assemble evidence for Medexa SIG request

Folks — Sara at Medexa asked for redaction examples, retention excerpt, and SOC 2 stub. Can we prepare the following by Monday: 

- Maya: redacted prompt_log_sample (remove timestamps beyond 30d, redact IPs/PII) and retention_policy_excerpt.txt
- Hannah: SOC2 Type II executive summary/scope (soc2-type2-stub.pdf) and a one-paragraph boilerplate we can share with procurement stating "no-training" by default and contractual options for addendum

Also include a short note explaining deletion timelines and the API/method we use to process on-demand deletes. Keep the redaction realistic; show an example of a PII scrub rule and a before/after snippet.

Thanks — J

From: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.com>
To: Sara Khan <sara.khan@medexa.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, alan.patel@medexa.com
Date: Sat, 12 Apr 2025 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — evidence bundle and redacted sample

Sara — attaching the files you requested. Quick highlights below and in the attachments: 

- retention_policy_excerpt.txt: We retain raw request/response payloads for 30 days (hosted API) to support debugging, abuse detection, and security investigations. Aggregated metrics (token counts, latency histograms) retained 180 days. Backups are retained for up to 90 days; deletion requests are processed to remove data from primary stores and next backup window.

- prompt_log_sample_redacted.txt: Attached is a realistic, redacted sample. We replace email addresses, phone numbers, SSNs with "[REDACTED]" and strip full names. We include a before/after snippet and a short note on the automated redaction pipeline (regex + ML-assisted PII detection + human review for flagged items).

- encryption & access control: All customer data at rest is encrypted with customer-managed keys for Private deployments, and KMS-managed keys for Hosted. Access requires RBAC and an audit trail; only a small SRE on-call group can request unredacted logs for security investigations and such access is logged and reviewed quarterly.

- soc2-type2-stub.pdf: Executive summary attached for procurement; full report available under NDA.

Attachments: prompt_log_sample_redacted.txt, retention_policy_excerpt.txt, soc2-type2-stub.pdf

Let me know if you want a short addendum template we can prefill for Medexa (legal will need to sign).

—Maya
Maya Srinivasan
Senior Product Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Khan <sara.khan@medexa.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: alan.patel@medexa.com, maya.srinivasan@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Apr 2025 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — clarification on prompt/log retention and training

Thanks, Maya and Jonas — the attachments are helpful. Two quick clarifications for procurement/legal: 

1) If a customer requests deletion of logs prior to the 30-day retention window (e.g., immediate deletion for a sensitive dataset), do you support on-demand deletion and can you provide evidence of deletion (audit trail)?

2) For the contractual "no-training" addendum: will Redwood commit to a clause preventing any use of customer data for model training or evaluation, and will that be enforceable across Hosted plans? We may ask for DocuSign-ready language.

Alan (procurement) — can you advise if we need anything else from Redwood to move forward?

Best,
Sara

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sara Khan <sara.khan@medexa.com>, alan.patel@medexa.com
Cc: maya.srinivasan@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Apr 2025 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — clarification on prompt/log retention and training

Sara / Alan — short answers: 

1) On-demand deletion: Yes. We expose a deletion API and a portal function for enterprise customers to submit deletion requests. Deletions are handled within 72 hours on the primary store and reflected in the next backup cycle; we attach an audit entry (request id + timestamp + operator) that can be exported. We can provide a sample audit log entry (redacted) as evidence.

2) No-training contractual addendum: Yes — Legal can provide DocuSign-ready language that commits Redwood not to use Medexa data for training, evaluation, or model improvement. For Hosted customers we support this via an enterprise addendum; for Private or Dedicated deployments the default operations already isolate customer data. I've looped in Alan for procurement steps.

Next steps: 
- Legal (Redwood) will prepare the addendum and DocuSign link (we've included a placeholder in related_links).
- We'll provide the sample audit log entry and the redacted prompt sample attached earlier as proof-of-concept for your Security team.

If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min call this week to walk Legal/Procurement through the addendum and timelines.

Thanks — J

Attachments: soc2-type2-stub.pdf
